block.rationale: Fresh verification block. The single holder below exercises every gap the original (stETH-only, single-request) suite left: multi-asset emission (a stETH leg AND a native-ETH leg from one oracle), multi-request summing on a real fork (two stETH requests), and the native-ETH payout branch. All three requests are pending at this block (each userNonce is above its asset's nextLockedNonce). Requests can be claimed by the owner at any time; the pin keeps them reproducible.

instance.note: Mainnet-only — Kelp's LRTWithdrawalManager exists only on Ethereum. Standalone (non-meta) adapter. Multi-asset: discovers payout assets at runtime via lrtConfig().getSupportedAssetList() and emits one credit leg per asset with non-zero owed that is also registered in NAV. stETH and native ETH are registered on the dev NAV; ETHx uses a custom feed the dev deploy.sh skips, so an ETHx request would be dropped from getOraclePositions (still readable via getOracleBalanceForAsset). positionId = "" (account-global); protocolId = keccak256('kelp-withdrawal'); positionKind = Supplied.

holders.label: MULTI_ASSET
notes: Two open stETH requests (nonces 7177 + 7203) summed into one stETH leg, plus one open native-ETH request (nonce 5937) as a second leg → getOraclePositions emits TWO legs from one oracle (the multi-asset path).
All three requests are pending at the fork block: each userNonce exceeds its asset's nextLockedNonce (stETH 7098, native ETH 5831), so none is claimable yet.
No ETHx request — and ETHx is not registered on the dev NAV (custom feed) — so no ETHx leg; the registered-vs-unregistered drop is covered in the unit test.

legs_at_fork_block.ground_truth: userAssociatedNonces(stETH, holder) => (1,3); sum of getUserWithdrawalRequest(stETH, holder, i).expectedAssetAmount for i in {0,1}

ground_truth.method: live LRTWithdrawalManager reads (NOT a Python re-derivation)
ground_truth.detail: Both legs are pinned against the real Kelp LRTWithdrawalManager at the fork block. stETH leg == sum of expectedAssetAmount over the holder's two open stETH requests; native-ETH leg == the single open native-ETH request's expectedAssetAmount. getOraclePositions emits exactly these two legs (ETHx skipped: no request + unregistered), each with protocolId == keccak256('kelp-withdrawal'), positionId == "" (account-global), PositionKind.Supplied, balanceOracle == address(this). Multi-request summing within an asset, multi-asset emission, the claimed-front-skip (deque pop), the 256 cap, and the registered-vs-unregistered drop are also covered with mocks in the unit test (test/balances/protocols/KelpWithdrawalQueueBalanceAdapter.t.sol).
